conventions: Run prep, embedded in every eval prompt: copy the named fixture context repo into <run-dir>/outputs/<repo-name>/, `git init` the copy, `git config user.name "<fixture person display name>" && git config user.email "<fixture person email>"`, stage every fixture file including dotfiles, commit as `fixture baseline`, then operate with the copy as cwd. Before acting, save a sorted SHA-256 manifest of every copied fixture file outside `.git/`, the exact HEAD, and `git status --short` outside the copied repo; repeat all three after acting. Use only the copied repo and run directory. Never read or write ~/.gtm, any real context repo, home-directory config, or any path outside <run-dir>, except the explicitly supplied skill and fixture source paths. Never create machine state, registries, pins, or state files. Every eval has complete inputs and an empty `user_replies` array: any assistant question or approval gate is an automatic contractual failure. Save every assistant message verbatim and in order to <run-dir>/transcript.md; the position echo must precede any preliminary or final classification. Record every shell command verbatim in <run-dir>/command-log.txt; any Git inspection must use `git -C <repo-root>`. Keep all run evidence outside the copied context repo. Baseline arms must not invoke or consult any installed skill; with-skill arms may use the supplied gtm-account-segmentation skill and installed siblings. Eval dirs are named eval-<ID>-<descriptive-name>, with outputs in run-1/outputs/. These harness requirements live only here, never in shipping SKILL.md.

evals.prompt: I’m at the root of our Signalforge GTM context repo. Segment Helix Metals (`helixmetals.example`) against the visible ICPs. Supplied facts: 1,800 employees; four owned production sites in Sweden and Germany; an internal operations-analytics team; a Snowflake warehouse; and an active plant-performance standardization program. It manufactures industrial components and owns its plants. Use only supplied facts and one visible qualified ICP label or `no-match`. Explain why the chosen label wins, include confidence and `needs_review`, and do not ask questions, enrich the account, or write anything.
evals.expected_output: A question-free response whose working line precedes classification, assigns exactly industrial-analytics-teams with high confidence and needs_review false despite the ICP's own maintenance backlog, includes every fixed one-off field and fixed metadata field with repo-relative sources, and explicitly reports no side effects. Fixture bytes, HEAD, and clean status remain unchanged.
expectations: O1-O3 exact one-off fields, label, rationale, and entity-level calibration

evals.prompt:
I’m at the root of our OrbitPay GTM context repo. Segment this complete routing table against visible ICPs using one exact qualified label or `no-match` per account. Use only these facts, ask zero questions, and write nothing.

| account | website | supplied facts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NordPay Bank | nordpay.example | Licensed digital bank in Sweden and Finland; 34 internal fraud analysts; case backlog after a monitoring-system migration |
| Kestrel Commerce | kestrel.example | B2B commerce platform embedding business accounts and payments; internal risk operations; direct API; launching in Germany |
| Silver Birch Advisory | silverbirch.example | Consulting agency reselling third-party payment tools; no operating license; no owned embedded-finance product |
| Unknown Harbor | unknownharbor.example | Financial-services company; operating model, license, team, product, and markets unknown |

Start with the fixed bulk summary, then return every account once with all fixed one-off fields. Confidence and `needs_review` must reflect each account’s evidence gaps rather than any ICP maintenance backlog.
evals.expected_output: A question-free bulk response beginning with counts regional-digital-banks 1, embedded-finance-platforms 1, no-match 2, low-confidence 1, review-needed 1, plus common evidence and questions. NordPay and Kestrel match their exact ICPs; Silver Birch is a high-confidence no-match with no review due to explicit disqualifiers; Unknown Harbor is the only low-confidence needs_review row. Every row and metadata field is present; no side effects occur.
expectations: B1-B5 exact summary order, counts, rows, labels, and account-level calibration

evals.prompt: I’m in the `emea` child of our Cloudmason GTM context repo. Segment Baltic Ledger (`balticledger.example`) against the ICPs visible here. Supplied facts: EEA-regulated digital bank; 1,200 employees; dedicated cloud-controls team; active DORA remediation program; operations in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Respect nearest same-stem precedence and keep non-colliding inherited ICPs visible. Return exactly one label with every fixed one-off and metadata field. Ask no questions and make no changes.
evals.expected_output: A question-free child-position response that reports root and child org sources; reports root enterprise as overridden by child enterprise while root mid-market remains visible; assigns exactly emea/enterprise, not enterprise or mid-market; uses high confidence and needs_review false from complete account evidence; and explicitly reports no side effects. Fixture bytes and Git state remain unchanged.
expectations: P1-P3 exact child visibility, qualified label, sources, and calibration
